2. The Authorities of the State of Andhra Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure
Corporation Limited, are aggrieved by the order dated 02.05.2018 passed by the High Cou

entities.text:
Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure
Corporation Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
rt for the States of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, whereby their revision petition challenging an order of the Executing Court, regarding payment of statutory interest to the respondent-land owners has been turned down, primarily on the ground that the issues sought to be raised were barred by the principle of res judicata.
3.

The land measuring about 336.75 cents was acquired for the establishment of a Pelletization and Sponge Iron Plant in Kakinada, for which the Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.63,000/- per acre.

The land owners sought a reference under Section 18 of the Land Special Tahsildar For Land ... vs Chelikani Cheeranjeevi (Died )Thr Lrs ... on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101393903/
1 Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short the Act), whereupon the Reference Court enhanced the compensation to Rs.97,650/- per acre, along with solatium and additional market value.

entities.text: Land Special Tahsildar For Land ... vs Chelikani Cheeranjeevi (Died )Thr Lrs
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Reference Court, however, expressly denied the land owners interest on additional market value and solatium.

4. The land owners being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Reference Court,
approached the High Court.
It appears that the appellants also filed cross-objections.
All the appeals and cross-objections came to be decided by the High Court vide a common judgment dated 13.08.2002, whereby the appeal of the land owners was allowed in the following terms:
This Court is of the considered view that taking the sale consideration into consideration, 50% deduction from Rs.38,800/- would be appropriate.
Therefore, we hold that the claimants in the above appeals are entitled to the compensation at the rate of Rs.1,69,400/- per acre.
In addition to the above amount, they are entitled to the statutory benefits.
(emphasis applied)

5. The respondent-land owners thereafter filed execution proceedings to recover the compensation amount as awarded by the High Court, and a dispute arose therein, before the Executing Court, as to whether or not they are entitled to interest as per Section 34 of the Act.
The Executing Court held the respondents to be entitled to such benefit.
The appellants then approached the High Court, but their revision petitions have been dismissed by the impugned order observing that the objections raised by them are barred by res judicata.
The High Court has said so for the reason that vide judgment dated 13.08.2002, the operative part whereof has been reproduced above, the respondents have been held entitled to the statutory benefits.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants strongly relies upon a Constitution Bench decision of this Court in Gurpreet Singh vs. Union of India, (2006) 8 SCC 457, to urge that since the Reference Court had specifically denied the claim for interest on solatium and additional market value, no such benefit can be granted by the Executing Court.

entities.text: Gurpreet Singh vs. Union of India, (2006) 8 SCC 457
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He relies upon the well settled principle that the Executing Court cannot go behind a decree.
7. In our considered view, the plea taken by the appellants is wholly misconceived and has been rightly rejected.

Once the High Court, in addition to the enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs.1,69,400/- per acre, held the land owners entitled to statutory benefits, it necessarily means that the respondents were granted additional market value under Section 23 as well as interest as per Section 34 of the Act.
Both these statutory benefits were admissible to the land owners in view of the judgment dated 13.08.2002, which has admittedly attained finality.
It is not a case of award of interest on arrears of interest as erroneously misconstrued by the appellants.
There is thus no error committed by the Executing Court or the High Court in rejecting the objections raised by the appellants.
The Executing Court will make the necessary calculations expeditiously.
8. The appeals are, accordingly, dismissed.
9. All pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
